findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext ignores the passed context entirely and returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), fabricating the contract that it 'has this logger's context plus the given context'. Any test that sets attributes on a TestLogger and then calls FromContext(ctx) silently gets a fresh empty logger instead of one carrying the parent's context, so tests using the new LoggerMiddleware.FromContext path validate against a fabricated logger, not the real contextual-logger behavior

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx) to *log.ConcreteLogger and silently falls back to d.New() on failure, an implementation the interface contract does not sanction. If infra/log's FromContext ever returns a different concrete wrapper type, plugin request logs lose all contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsUID) with no error or warning, degrading the grafana-data-egress log payload that this PR is restructuring around

[ADVISORY] NewContextualLoggerMiddleware is inserted after NewMetricsMiddleware but the MetricsMiddleware no longer applies instrumentContext, so streaming endpoints (SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream), which neither middleware instruments, lose contextual logging attributes that previously came from InstrumentationMiddleware's instrumentContext for the non-streaming paths only — however, callers reaching LoggerMiddleware when skipLogger short-circuits (skip_cookies/LoggerMiddleware disabled) now get a context with attributes attached that nothing consumes, adding per-request []any allocation with no effect. Every plugin request pays the instrumentContext slice allocation and WithContextualAttributes wrapper even when the downstream LoggerMiddleware is disabled via cfg, a new unconditional per-request cost on a hot path

[BUG] logRequest previously appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx) traceID to the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line; the diff deletes that code and no replacement adds traceID (the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext also does not add it), so 'grafana-data-egress' log lines permanently lose their trace ID. Operators correlating plugin egress logs with traces lose the traceID field on every plugin request completion log; this is an acceptance criterion of the logging behavior that the refactor silently drops.

[ADVISORY] No test file for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware exists anywhere in the diff (instrumentation_middleware_test.go was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go, not extended), so the new endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname contextual-attribute behavior is entirely unverified. A regression in instrumentContext (e.g. dropping dsUID or misnaming a key) ships silently; the renamed metrics test only covers metrics, not the extracted logging behavior the rename moved out.

[ADVISORY] The logger is still constructed with the name log.New("plugin.instrumentation") while the diff renames the instrumentation concept to metrics, leaving the log label stale on a renamed path. Users grepping logs/dashboards by the 'plugin.instrumentation' logger name see naming that no longer matches the code organization, making the rename's intent (instrumentation == metrics) harder to follow.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext ignores the passed context entirely and returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), so any contextual attributes present in ctx are silently discarded in test doubles implementing the new interface method. Tests that rely on FromContext propagating contextual attributes through the Logger interface will pass with the fake while production behavior (attribute propagation) is untested, hiding regressions in the exact code path this PR adds.

[ADVISORY] ContextualLoggerMiddleware passes streaming endpoints (SubscribeStream, PublishStream, RunStream) through without instrumentContext, an asymmetry carried over from the old InstrumentationMiddleware rather than addressed while the logic was being relocated. Streaming plugin requests log 'Plugin Request Completed' without endpoint/pluginId/dsName context, so the new contextual-logger feature is inconsistently applied across the endpoints the middleware stack serves.

[ADVISORY] The PR is stated as a chore rename of instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware, but it introduces an entirely new ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus a new FromContext method on the plugins log.Logger interface, work that is not traceable to the stated intent. Reviewers and release-note readers treat this as a no-op rename; a behavior-affecting change (log attribute enrichment moved out of the metrics middleware into a new middleware and interface expansion) ships under a chore label, bypassing the scrutiny a behavioral PR would receive.

[BUG] The removed logParams block silently drops the traceID attribute from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, and no other code in this diff re-adds it. Operators lose the ability to correlate plugin request completion logs with traces (the traceID field disappears from grafana-data-egress log records), a behavioral logging regression hidden inside a chore PR.

[ADVISORY] ContextualLoggerMiddleware decorates only QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics, leaving SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream without contextual logger attributes, so the plugin/request-detail invariant is not enforced on streaming paths. Stream handlers downstream that call FromContext get a logger missing pluginId/dsUID/uname, producing inconsistent log attribution for streaming plugin requests versus request/response ones.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of a logger sharing the receiver's captured Logs state, so assertions against logs written through the FromContext path will not see entries written via the context-derived logger. Any test using the fake and asserting on captured logs after a call goes through FromContext silently observes zero calls, masking real logging regressions the interface change is meant to catch.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts to *log.ConcreteLogger and falls back to d.New() on failure, an unchecked downcast whose fallback silently discards the requested context instead of preserving the wrapper semantics. If the infra logger implementation changes or returns a different concrete type, every FromContext call silently returns a logger with no contextual attributes and no compile-time or log-time signal that the enrichment stopped working.

[ADVISORY] The middleware stack wires the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware for every plugin client unconditionally, with no configuration or feature-flag gate, expanding the runtime work per plugin request (context decoration plus interface indirection) beyond the rename the PR claims. If the contextual attribute enrichment misbehaves or regresses performance on high-QPS query paths, it cannot be disabled without a code deploy, and the change lands as part of a 'chore' that operators will not scrutinize.

[BUG] The 'Plugin Request Completed' log line permanently loses the traceID field: logRequest no longer appends tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx) and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext does not add a traceID attribute either. Operators correlating plugin request failures with traces lose the traceID on grafana-data-egress logs that previously carried it; dashboards/alerts keyed on that field silently go empty after deploy.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() and ignores the receiver, so attributes accumulated in the context produce a logger object that no test holds a reference to. Any test asserting on middleware-emitted log lines via a captured TestLogger now observes an empty logger: the contextual-attribute path (the entire point of ContextualLoggerMiddleware) is green in CI only because assertions target a different instance than the one written to — a stand-in guard that can pass while the real wiring is unexercised.

[ADVISORY] Adding FromContext to the exported plog.Logger interface is an unversioned breaking change: every out-of-tree implementation of plugins/log.Logger stops compiling, and the new method's semantics ('returns this logger's context plus the given context' per the docstring) are contradicted by the in-tree TestLogger implementation, which returns an unrelated fresh logger. External plugin/logger implementers break at compile time on upgrade, and readers of the interface contract get two conflicting definitions of FromContext — the fake should mirror the wrapper's semantics (carry existing state) or the docstring is wrong.

[ADVISORY] The middleware stack now runs two middlewares (MetricsMiddleware, then ContextualLoggerMiddleware) where one previously did both jobs, and LoggerMiddleware still exists as a third logging-adjacent middleware — the contextual-logger concern now lives in a new parallel path rather than consolidating into LoggerMiddleware. The next person adding a request attribute must know to touch ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext, not LoggerMiddleware.logRequest or MetricsMiddleware; the old single-place contract (MetricsMiddleware 'enriches the context... should live at the top of the stack') is gone but its docstring remnants in metrics_middleware.go still reference the instrumentation role, inviting edits at the wrong site.

[BUG] The refactor silently drops the "traceID" attribute from plugin request completion logs: the previous logRequest appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) to logParams, and the new version removed both the tracing import and the traceID field with no replacement in the new logParams list. Every 'Plugin Request Completed' log line loses its trace ID, breaking the existing trace-to-log correlation workflow operators and dashboards rely on; this behavior regression was not part of the stated rename objective and there is no evidence of explicit human acceptance for it.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated objective is a chore rename of instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware, but the diff smuggles in a behavior change: a brand-new NewContextualLoggerMiddleware is inserted into the middleware stack and the plog.Logger interface gains a required FromContext method — an objective change (contextual logging redesign) presented under a rename-only title. Reviewers and downstream consumers accepting 'just a rename' unknowingly accept a new middleware in the hot request path and a breaking interface change; any out-of-tree plog.Logger implementation fails to compile against the new interface member without ever having been notified of the feature change.

[ADVISORY] logRequest now sources pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname from the context via m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of taking req.PluginContext, so the log fields depend on the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware being positioned above LoggerMiddleware in the stack. Any future reordering of CreateMiddlewares (or use of LoggerMiddleware in a stack lacking the new middleware, e.g. other callers constructing client middleware lists) silently produces 'Plugin Request Completed' lines missing pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname, with no compile-time or startup guard; the previously direct request-derived fields become implicit cross-middleware coupling.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently degrades to d.New() (dropping all contextual attributes) when the infra logger's FromContext result does not type-assert to *log.ConcreteLogger, converting a wiring mismatch into lost log context rather than an error. If the wrapped logger ever returns a non-ConcreteLogger implementation, plugin request logs lose pluginId/dsName/uname attributes with no error or warning, making the failure mode invisible to operators debugging plugin requests.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext ignores its argument and returns a fresh NewTestLogger(), so tests exercising the new contextual-logging path assert against a different logger instance than the one whose context was instrumented. Any test that instruments a context, then calls FromContext expecting the Calls/Message captured on the original TestLogger, silently reads from an unrelated fresh logger and records nothing — masking regressions in the contextual-logging behavior this PR introduces.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so any code under test that logs through the context writes to a discarded logger instance. Tests that wire this fake into the new FromContext(ctx) flow (e.g. via LoggerMiddleware) and then assert on f.Calls/f.Message inspect a logger that never received the log call — the assertions pass vacuously against an empty logger or, worse, tests must reach into an unrelated instance, giving false confidence that logging behavior was verified.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in this diff is a mechanical constructor rename in the renamed metrics middleware test; no assertion in any test in the diff exercises the new behavior (contextual logger attached via instrumentContext moved into the new middleware, or LoggerMiddleware's new m.logger.FromContext(ctx) call). TestInstrumentationMiddleware continues to pass while the contextual-logger responsibility it implicitly covered (instrumentContext enriching ctx) was moved out of this middleware into a new untested middleware — a regression in the logger context enrichment (e.g. dropped attributes) would leave every existing test green.

[ADVISORY] The refactor drops the traceID attribute that logRequest previously attached to every 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, and neither ContextualLoggerMiddleware nor instrumentContext adds it. Operators correlating grafana-data-egress logs with traces lose the traceID field they previously had on every plugin request log; dashboards/alerts keyed on that field silently return nothing after this change, with no error anywhere.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the type assertion to *log.ConcreteLogger fails, discarding the request context's contextual attributes with no log or error. If infra/log ever returns a non-ConcreteLogger (custom wrapper or future change), every plugin request log silently loses endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname context instead of failing loudly, and the regression is invisible because the call still 'succeeds'.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), so any code path exercised under the test logger silently routes logs to an object the test does not hold a reference to. Tests asserting on TestLogger.Logs will see zero calls for log lines emitted via FromContext (e.g. LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed'), making assertions pass vacuously or fail confusingly, while production behavior is untested.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

This is a concrete, diff-grounded per-request overhead concern. However, the finding’s claim about streaming endpoints “losing” contextual attributes is not supported: the prior `InstrumentationMiddleware` also did not instrument `SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream` (they were pass-through and `instrumentContext` was only applied in `instrumentPluginRequest` for non-streaming endpoints), and the new middleware similarly does not instrument streaming endpoints.

There is no new `*_test.go` added for this middleware, and the renamed `instrumentation_middleware_test.go` -> `metrics_middleware_test.go` only follows the metrics middleware rename and no longer covers the extracted `instrumentContext` logic (which was removed from the metrics middleware). This makes the new contextual-attribute enrichment unverified by tests in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go the new method `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` explicitly discards the provided context and returns a fresh logger. Given the Logger interface contract added in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go (`FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` intended to create a contextual logger), this fake does not model the production behavior implemented in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go (`grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` wraps `d.l.FromContext(ctx)`). This can weaken tests by not exercising/validating contextual attribute propagation through `FromContext`, but it is not a direct runtime defect in production code.

adjudication.rationale: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only calls instrumentContext for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream are pass-throughs (contextual_logger_middleware.go). That creates a diff-grounded asymmetry in applying contextual logger enrichment across client endpoints. However, the finding’s specific claim that streaming endpoints will log "Plugin Request Completed" without endpoint/pluginId context is not directly supported by this diff because LoggerMiddleware’s logRequest wrapper is only used for those four non-streaming endpoints in the shown changes.

Reviewers and release-note readers treat this as a no-op rename; a behavior-affecting change (log attribute enrichment moved out of the metrics middleware into a new middleware and interface expansion) ships under a chore label, bypassing the scrutiny a behavioral PR would receive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does more than a rename: it adds a new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (new file) and changes middleware composition to include it (`CreateMiddlewares` adds `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()`), and it expands the `pkg/plugins/log.Logger` interface with `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger`, requiring updates to implementations (`fake.go`, `logger.go`). It also moves contextual log enrichment out of the former instrumentation middleware by deleting `instrumentContext` usage in the renamed `metrics_middleware.go` and instead logging via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` in `logger_middleware.go`. These are behavioral/API-surface changes beyond a no-op rename and warrant higher scrutiny even if not a functional defect.

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, the explicit addition of traceID via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and `logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID)` was removed, and the remaining logParams no longer include any trace identifier. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds endpoint/plugin/datasource/user attributes via `log.WithContextualAttributes` and does not add traceID. The code now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` (new Logger method) to potentially inject trace context, but the diff does not verify that a `traceID` field will still be present on the log record, so this is a concrete regression risk that should be confirmed/tests updated.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, `instrumentContext` is applied only in `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics`; `SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, and `RunStream` just delegate to `m.next` without adding contextual attributes. Meanwhile `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, meaning it relies on context-enriched logging. The diff therefore supports the concern that streaming paths will not receive the same plugin/request attributes unless some other middleware adds them, creating inconsistent log attribution rather than a direct functional break.

This means any logs emitted via f.FromContext(ctx).Info/Warn/Error will be captured in a different TestLogger instance, not in the original f's Logs fields, violating the interface intent (“has this logger's context plus the given context”) and breaking/invalidating tests that expect the receiver to record calls when the new FromContext path is used (e.g., LoggerMiddleware now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info).

This is a diff-grounded robustness/compatibility concern: if infra/log ever returns a different Logger implementation, contextual enrichment would be silently dropped with no signal. (Similarly, TestLogger.FromContext ignores the provided context and returns a fresh logger.)
